gloss: scatter, disperse; be scattered; spread abroad, overflow
summary: To come apart and spread out in every direction: an army routed or sent home, a flock with no shepherd, the nations from Babel, Israel among the peoples. Moses’ cry as the ark set out, “Rise, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered” (Num 10:35; Psa 68:2), uses the qal; in the hiphil it is chiefly Yahweh scattering a people in judgment, “among the nations and among the lands” (Deu 4:27; Ezk 12:15), with the promise to gather them again (Deu 30:3; Ezk 28:25). Christ took “strike the shepherd, and the flock will scatter” (Zec 13:7) for himself and his disciples (Mat 26:31). Arabic fāḍa “overflow, spread abroad” and fawḍā “in dispersion, with no chief” answer to it, as does the use of springs and cities spreading out with plenty (Pro 5:16; Zec 1:17).

words.summary: Qal and niphal, of people coming apart and spreading out; hiphil, of scattering them (and, intransitively, of their dispersing). The polel, pilpel and hithpolel (Jer 23:29; Job 16:12; Hab 3:6) are the regular reduplicated stems of a hollow root and are analysed so in the text, though some dictionaries file them under a root פצץ: they mean breaking into pieces that fly apart, scattering seen from the thing broken. The shattering rests on three verses, and no cognate yet shares it surely: Akkadian paʾāṣu “break up”, whose adjective also means “dispersed”, is possible only.

senses.definition: Of enemies or a beaten force breaking up and running in every direction, so that no two are left together.

evidence.note: As the ark set out: “Rise, Yahweh, וְיָפֻצוּ your enemies, and let those who hate you flee from your face”: scattering set beside fleeing.
Moses’ words taken up: “Let God arise, let his enemies scatter, and let those who hate him flee from his face.”
The Ammonites left alive “scattered, and two among them were not left together”.

senses.gloss: be scattered, of a flock without a shepherd
senses.definition: Of sheep, and of the people as sheep, straying apart for want of a shepherd to keep them together.

evidence.note: “They scattered for lack of a shepherd, and became food for every beast of the field, and they scattered.”
“Strike the shepherd, and the flock will scatter.”
Christ quotes Zec 13:7 of himself and his disciples on the night he was betrayed: “the sheep of the flock will be scattered.”
Fulfilled: “then all the disciples left him and fled.”
The prince is not to take the people’s inheritance, “so that my people are not scattered, each from his possession”.

senses.gloss: disperse, go off in all directions
senses.definition: Of people breaking up and going their own ways, without defeat: an army sent home, or men sent out among the people.

evidence.note: Joab blew the shofar “and they dispersed from the city, each to his tent”.
“Disperse among the people and say to them, Bring me each his ox.”
“Let us build a city and a tower … lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth”: what Babel was built against.
בַּת־פוּצַי, “the daughter of my scattered ones”, bringing Yahweh’s offering from beyond the rivers of Cush: the passive participle of those dispersed.

stems.gloss: be scattered, be dispersed; spread out

senses.definition: Of soldiers breaking away from their king or leader when the battle is lost.

evidence.note: Zedekiah overtaken in the plains of Jericho, “and all his army was scattered from him”.
If Gedaliah is killed, “all Judah who are gathered to you will be scattered”: scattered against gathered.

senses.definition: Of Israel as sheep scattered on the hills and over the land, with no shepherd seeking them.

evidence.note: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills, like sheep that have no shepherd.”
The shepherds have not sought Yahweh, “and all their flock is scattered”.
“My flock was scattered over all the face of the earth, and no one searched or sought.”
Yahweh will seek out his sheep and deliver them “from all the places where they were scattered”.

senses.definition: Of a people spread among other peoples and lands, the state from which Yahweh promises to gather them.

evidence.note: “Afterward the clans of the Canaanites were spread abroad.”
“I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you out of the lands where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.”
Gathered from the peoples among whom they were scattered, “they will dwell on their own land that I gave to my servant Jacob”.
Egypt too, gathered after forty years from the peoples where they were scattered.

senses.definition: Of a battle spreading over the whole face of a country.

evidence.note: “The battle was spread there over the face of all the land” (נָפֹצֶת, the read form).

senses.gloss: scatter a people among the nations
senses.definition: Yahweh’s act of judgment, breaking up a people and spreading them among other peoples and lands; from Babel, and as the covenant’s curse on Israel’s unfaithfulness, with the promise to gather them again.

evidence.note: “Yahweh scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.”
“Yahweh will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations.”
“From one end of the earth to the other”, there to serve gods of wood and stone.
Yahweh “will gather you again from all the peoples where Yahweh your God has scattered you”.
Nehemiah recalls the word to Moses: “If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples.”
“When I scatter them among the nations and disperse them (זֵרִיתִי) among the lands”: the standing pair.
“According to their ways and their deeds I judged them.”
“Like chaff blown away by the wind of the wilderness.”
“Like an east wind I will scatter them before the enemy.”
Yahweh will make a full end of all the nations where he scattered Israel, but not of Israel.
Egypt scattered the same way.
Yahweh empties the land and scatters its inhabitants.
Of Simeon and Levi: “I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.”

senses.definition: Drive a foe apart in battle, of Yahweh’s arrows and lightning and of a wind that blows them away.

evidence.note: “He sent out arrows and scattered them; lightning, and routed them.”
“Flash lightning and scatter them; send out your arrows and rout them.”
“You will winnow them, the wind will carry them off, and the storm will scatter them.”
The enemy “stormed out to scatter me”.
Terrors “scatter him at his heels”: drive him every way.

senses.definition: Of Israel’s shepherds, who scattered Yahweh’s flock by neglect and violence instead of keeping it together.

evidence.note: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!”
“You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and have not attended to them.”
The strong sheep push the weak with side and shoulder and horn “until you have scattered them abroad”.

senses.definition: Spread something out over a space: seed sown broadcast, a cloud, wind or light, the overflowing of anger.

evidence.note: The farmer levels the ground “and scatters dill and sows cumin”.
“He scatters the cloud of his lightning.”
The way “the east wind is spread over the earth”.
“Scatter abroad the overflowings of your anger.”

senses.definition: Of a people going off in every direction.

evidence.note: “So the people scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.”
Saul’s people were scattering from him while he waited for Samuel; Saul says the same with נָפַץ in 1Sa 13:11.

senses.definition: Break something hard so that its pieces fly apart.

evidence.note: “Is not my word like fire, and like a hammer that shatters rock?”

senses.definition: Break a man apart, as Job says God has done to him.

evidence.note: “I was at ease, and he broke me apart; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces.”

senses.definition: Of the ancient mountains breaking apart when God stands and looks.

evidence.note: “He looked and made the nations start; the everlasting mountains were shattered, the ancient hills sank down.”

evidence.locator: Num.10.35, יָפֻצוּ → διασκορπισθήτωσαν; Neh.1.8, אָפִיץ → διασκορπιῶ; Ezk.28.25, נָפֹצוּ → διεσκορπίσθησαν; διασκορπίζω renders פּוּץ ×10

evidence.note: Zec 13:7 quoted: “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock διασκορπισθήσεται.”
Christ to die “to gather together into one the children of God τὰ διεσκορπισμένα”: the gathering of the scattered.

evidence.locator: Gen.11.8, וַיָּפֶץ → διέσπειρεν; Deu.4.27, וְהֵפִיץ → διασπερεῖ; διασπείρω renders פּוּץ ×19

evidence.note: The ecclesia at Jerusalem “were all scattered (διεσπάρησαν) through the regions of Judea and Samaria”.
“You will be scattered (σκορπισθῆτε), each to his own, and will leave me alone”: Zec 13:7 again.
The wolf “scatters” the sheep the hireling leaves.
“He who does not gather with me scatters”: gathering and scattering opposed.

parallels.note: “Disperse, winnow”: scatter among the nations and disperse among the lands.
“Flee”: the scattered enemies flee from Yahweh’s face.
“Drive away”: the shepherds scattered the flock and drove them away.
“Divide”: Simeon and Levi divided in Jacob and scattered in Israel.

opposites.note: “Gather”: Yahweh gathers from the lands where he scattered them.

evidence.note: Those gathered to Gedaliah would be scattered.

phrases.gloss: scatter among the nations and disperse among the lands
over the face of the whole earth
scattered like sheep that have no shepherd
rise, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered

words.summary: Used twice, of springs and of cities spreading out with plenty. It may be the same verb as פּוּץ “scatter”, seen from the thing that spreads: Arabic fāḍa has both senses, “overflow” and “spread abroad, disperse”.

senses.definition: Of water running out beyond its source, and of cities spreading out, full of good.

evidence.note: “Should your springs be spread abroad outside, streams of water in the streets?” Beside פַּלְגֵי־מָיִם, “channels of water”.
“My cities will again spread out (תְּפוּצֶינָה) with good, and Yahweh will again comfort Zion.”

words.summary: The hiphil participle used as a noun: one who scatters. In Pro 25:18 it stands beside sword and arrow as a weapon, a club that smashes; whether that is this root or a spelling of מַפֵּץ “war club” from נפץ (Jer 51:20) is not clear.

senses.definition: An enemy who comes to scatter a city’s people.

evidence.note: “A scatterer has come up against you; guard the rampart, watch the road.”

senses.definition: A weapon for smashing, named with sword and arrow.

evidence.note: “A club and a sword and a sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbour.”

words.summary: Once, in the plural with suffix, of the shepherds’ coming scattering; its form and its place in the sentence are unusual, and the sense rests on that one verse and the verb.

senses.definition: The shepherds’ own scattering, set beside their slaughter as the days now come.

evidence.note: “Wail, you shepherds … for your days for slaughter and your scatterings (וּתְפוֹצוֹתֵיכֶם) are fulfilled, and you will fall like a choice vessel.”

cognates.gloss: overflow, pour forth; spread abroad; (form IV, of a crowd) push on and disperse
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give fāḍa of water that “overflowed … flowed over the brink of the valley”, and of news that “spread abroad … among the people, like water”; ʾafāḍū min ʿArafāt is “they pushed on … with multitude” or “dispersed themselves from ʿArafāt”. It holds together the “overflow” of Pro 5:16 and Zec 1:17 and the “scatter, disperse” of the commoner verb. Arabic ḍ (ض), not ṣ (ص), stands behind צ.

evidence.note: afāḍū min ʿArafāt: pushed on with multitude, or dispersed themselves
a report spread abroad among the people

cognates.gloss: (people) in a state of dispersion; equals with no chief, none to collect them
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give qawm fawḍā as “a company of men who are equals, having no chief … or separated, or in a state of dispersion … having no commander, nor any to collect them together”, and of wild animals “in a state of dispersion, going to and fro”; it is said to be the plural of fāʾiḍ, and fayḍūḍā of root فيض is given as the same word. It answers closely to Israel “scattered … like sheep that have no shepherd” (1Ki 22:17; Ezk 34:5).

evidence.note: the same as fawḍā, under root فيض

cognates.gloss: break up, crush; (adjective) crushed, dispersed, stray
cognates.note: The verb is “break up, crush”, and its adjective is glossed “crushed; dispersed; stray”, which joins the shattering of the polel stems (Jer 23:29; Job 16:12; Hab 3:6) to the scattering of the rest. Possible only: its middle consonant is ʾ, not w, and Akkadian ṣ does not show which older sound stands behind צ.

doctrine.statement: Moses warned that if Israel were unfaithful Yahweh would scatter them among the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other (Deu 4:27; 28:64), and Nehemiah held Yahweh to that word (Neh 1:8). The same word promised the end of it: Yahweh would gather them from all the peoples where he had scattered them (Deu 30:3). Ezekiel says what the gathering is for: from the lands where they were scattered he will “give you the land of Israel”, and they will “dwell on their own land that I gave to my servant Jacob”, Yahweh being sanctified in them before the nations (Ezk 11:17; 28:25). Jeremiah adds that he will make a full end of the nations where he scattered them, but not of Israel (Jer 30:11). So the scattering is a judgment with a set end, and its end is a people gathered back to the land promised to the fathers.

Israel’s shepherds scattered Yahweh’s flock, and the sheep scattered for want of a shepherd (Jer 23:1–2; Ezk 34:5–6); Yahweh promised to seek them out from all the places where they were scattered and to set over them one shepherd, his servant David (Ezk 34:12, 23). Zechariah’s “strike the shepherd, and the flock will scatter” (Zec 13:7) Christ applied to himself on the night he was betrayed (Mat 26:31; Mrk 14:27), and it came to pass when all the disciples left him and fled (Mat 26:56). He is the shepherd who lays down his life where the hireling lets the wolf scatter the sheep (Jhn 10:11–12), and he died to gather into one the children of God scattered abroad (Jhn 11:52): the scattering of the flock is undone by the shepherd struck for it.

After the flood the nations were divided in the earth from the families of Noah’s sons (Gen 10:32). Men built a city and tower so as not to be scattered over the face of the whole earth (Gen 11:4), and Yahweh scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth and confused their language (Gen 11:8–9). The spread of the peoples across the earth is therefore Yahweh’s own act, at one place and time after the flood, among men of one family; Paul says the same: God “made of one blood all nations of men to dwell on all the face of the earth” (Act 17:26).

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (וְיָפֻצוּ, Num 10:35). The corpus keys the root פוצ, as the task gave it. BDB key q.cm.aa (פָּצַץ “break, shatter”, root פצצ) is claimed for the verb because its three tokens (Jer 23:29 יְפֹצֵץ, Job 16:12 וַיְפַצְפְּצֵנִי, Hab 3:6 וַיִּתְפֹּצְצוּ) are the regular polel, pilpel and hithpolel of a hollow root and the corpus analyses them under פוצ; review whether they should go to a separate פצץ entry. The priestly name הַפִּצֵּץ (1Ch 24:15, q.cm.ab) is not entered. Left out, as the corpus and BDB put them under נפץ (n.em.aa “disperse”): Gen 9:19 נָפְצָה “overspread”, 1Sa 13:11 נָפַץ “scattered from me”, Isa 11:12 נְפֻצוֹת “the dispersed of Judah”, and Jer 22:28 נָפוּץ “shattered vessel”; whoever writes נפץ should weigh whether נפץ II is a by-form of this root. Zero-token cross-reference keys m.da.ba and w.bi.ak are not named. The surface index tags every form of the root with all its keys, so lexicon-support’s use counts for the two פּוּץ words and מֵפִיץ overlap. Pro 25:18 מֵפִיץ “club” may be מַפֵּץ (n.el.ad, נפץ), kept here as a sense of מֵפִיץ. Jer 25:34 תְּפוֹצוֹתֵיכֶם: form unusual; kept as a noun. LXX: Zec 13:7 renders by ἐκσπάσατε, but Mat 26:31 follows the Hebrew with διασκορπισθήσεται; Nah 2:2 by ἐμφυσῶν; Jer 23:1 by ἀπολλύοντες. Not entered: Arabic fāṣa (فاص, with ṣ) “went away into the land”, tafāwuṣ “being separated one from another” (Lane p. 2458 n34818, p. 2471 n34957), a look-alike with the other sound behind צ; Jewish Aramaic נְפַץ and post-biblical Hebrew פּוּץ (Jastrow), the first another root, the second not a cognate. Not consulted: Ugaritic, Geʿez (Dillmann, Leslau), Syriac (the Peshitta has no cognate root in the brief). Open for review: (1) q.cm.aa claimed here; (2) the doctrine topics, especially the-good-shepherd’s reading of Zec 13:7 and Jhn 11:52.
